title: Interaction and non-Hermiticity controlled transmission in extended Su-Schrieffer-Heeger models
authors: Syeda Rafisa Rahaman, Shreekantha Sil, Nilanjan Bondyopadhaya
abstract: We study the transport characteristics of an extended version of the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) model with next-nearest-neighbor (NNN) interactions and non-Hermitian onsite energies. We observed that transport in such a system is significantly modified by the NNN interaction and the non-Hermitian terms. The transmission coefficient exhibits oscillatory behavior as the strength of the NNN interaction varies in a fixed-length chain. Moreover, the transmission coefficient also shows oscillation with system size for a fixed strength of the NNN interaction. We find that novel oscillatory behavior of the transmission coefficient, arising form the NNN interaction, is a unique feature of such a model and has not been reported previously. The presence of the non-Hermitian terms also enhances/reduces the transmission coefficient depending on the values of the other system parameters like intra-, inter- and NNN hopping. It appears from our study that both the NNN interaction and the non-Hermiticity introduce significant changes in the transport properties of the extended SSH chain, which are not observed in the standard Hermitian nearest-neighbour variant of the SSH model.
summary: This paper theoretically analyzes quantum transport through an extended Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model modified by NNN interactions and non-Hermiticity. It demonstrates that these additions induce unique oscillatory behaviors in the transmission coefficient, which are not present in simpler models. The findings highlight how engineered gain/loss can fundamentally alter the electronic properties of low-dimensional quantum systems.
main_problem: The study investigates how next-nearest-neighbor (NNN) interactions and non-Hermitian onsite energies modify quantum transport characteristics in an extended Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) model.
main_result: Both NNN interaction and non-Hermiticity introduce significant, novel oscillatory behaviors in the transmission coefficient, which are absent in standard Hermitian SSH models. The system can exhibit $T>1$ in certain broken symmetry regimes.
method: The analysis employs scattering matrix theory using the Green's function formalism to calculate the transmission coefficient ($T$) through the extended chain connected to semi-infinite leads.
model_or_system: The model is an extended SSH chain incorporating intra-, inter-, and NNN hopping terms, along with non-Hermitian onsite energies ($\epsilon_1, \epsilon_2$). The Hamiltonian describes this lattice structure coupled to external leads.
key_observables: Transmission coefficient ($T$), which measures quantum transparency; energy eigenvalues (real vs. imaginary) related to PT-symmetry breaking.
important_parameters: NNN interaction strength ($\delta_3$), system size ($N$), non-Hermitian onsite potentials ($\epsilon_1, \epsilon_2$), and hopping parameters ($\delta_1, \delta_2$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes elastic scattering within the middle wire region; calculations are based on solving the Schrödinger equation via Green's functions.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate $T$ vs. $\delta_3$ showing oscillations (interaction-induced transparency), $T$ vs. $N$ showing regular length oscillations, and comparisons of $T$ in PT-symmetric versus PT-broken regimes.
paper_structure: The paper systematically develops the Hamiltonian, presents numerical results varying $\delta_3$, then analyzes the effects of non-Hermiticity ($\epsilon$), contrasting topological and non-topological phases for both balanced gain-loss and pure loss/gain scenarios.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it extends SSH models—a canonical system in condensed matter physics—into non-Hermitian regimes, providing new insights into how engineered dissipation or gain can control quantum transport phenomena like transparency oscillations.
